Text: Cardiac function declines with age largely because of {{c1::atherosclerosis::vascular condition}}, a buildup of {{c2::cholesterol and calcium::two substances}} along the inner walls of blood vessels that forms plaque.
Back Extra: Mechanism: as plaque accumulates, blood flow through the affected vessels becomes restricted or blocked entirely.

Text: More than {{c1::60%::percentage}} of people older than {{c1::65 years::age}} have atherosclerotic disease.
Back Extra:
Distinguish: the age-related drop in heart rate is a baseline change; in a life-threatening illness the body still raises the heart rate to preserve blood pressure.

Pitfall: because cardiac muscle weakens with age, that faster rate may damage the heart, and combined with atherosclerosis of sufficient severity the damage could prove fatal.

Text:
Beyond atherosclerosis, aging weakens the older adult's heart in three ways:

{{c1::the heart rate decreases}}

{{c1::cardiac output declines}}

{{c1::the ability to increase cardiac output on demand diminishes}}
Back Extra:
Distinguish: the age-related drop in heart rate is a baseline change; in a life-threatening illness the body still raises the heart rate to preserve blood pressure.

Meaning: cardiac output is the amount of blood pumped by the heart each minute.

Why: the aging heart is left less able to cope with exercise or disease.

Text: Because the older adult's vascular system stiffens, blood vessels cannot dilate and contract effectively, so {{c1::diastolic::systolic or diastolic}} blood pressure {{c1::increases::increases or decreases}} and the heart must work harder against vascular resistance.
Back Extra: Pitfall: over time the increased workload can be detrimental to the heart itself, so stiff vessels are a slow-building cardiac problem, not just a blood pressure reading.

Text: Human blood cells originate in the bone marrow, but with advancing age that marrow is replaced by {{c1::fatty tissue}}.
Back Extra:
Why: losing marrow means losing the ability to manufacture new blood cells.

Pitfall: alone the change is not cause for alarm, but in a traumatic injury where a large volume of blood is lost quickly, the impeded ability to replace those cells can be devastating.

Text:
Classify each of the four ways aging changes the older adult's respiratory system:

Size of the airway: {{c1::increases::increases or decreases}}

Surface area of the alveoli: {{c1::decreases::increases or decreases}}

Elasticity of the lungs: {{c1::decreases::increases or decreases}}

Strength of the intercostal muscles and diaphragm: {{c1::decreases::increases or decreases}}
Back Extra:
Why: smaller alveolar surface, stiffer lungs, and weaker breathing muscles together make breathing more laborious for the older adult.

Cue: three of the four go down with age — the size of the airway is the lone item that goes up.

Text: {{c1::Vital capacity}} is the volume of air moved during {{c2::the deepest inspiration and expiration}}.
Back Extra: Pitfall: the age-related respiratory changes are gradual and usually go unnoticed, until a severe, life-threatening illness makes the lack of respiratory reserve pronounced.

Text: By age {{c1::75::age}}, an older adult's vital capacity has declined to about {{c1::50%::percentage}} of that of a young adult.
Back Extra: Pitfall: the aging chest is also more rigid yet more fragile — instead of bending and flexing under stress, the calcified rib cage is more susceptible to fracture.

Text:
With age, five protective features of the upper airway weaken:

{{c1::the cough reflex}}

{{c1::the gag reflex}}

{{c1::the ability to clear secretions}}

{{c1::the cilia that line the airway}}

{{c1::sensation within the airway}}
Back Extra: Why: losing all five at once is what makes an open upper airway hard to maintain in the older adult.

Text: As the structures protecting the upper airway lose function with age, the older adult is at greater risk of {{c1::aspiration}} and {{c1::airway obstruction}}.
Back Extra: Pitfall: the risk is a quiet one, because sensation within the airway also declines and the older adult may not register material sitting in the airway at all.
